node-1.label: Patient experienced chest pain and shortness of breath for 2 months

node-2.label: 32-year-old male with no cough, expectoration, or hemoptysis; no limb swelling or lump; no abdominal pain or weight loss; no history of tobacco smoking or other addictions

node-3.label: Vital signs: pulse rate 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 per minute, blood pressure 116/78 mmHg, oxygen saturation 95%

node-4.label: Chest examination showed a dull note on percussion and absent breath sounds in the entire right hemithorax, except for normal breath sounds in the right infraclavicular area

node-5.label: Chest radiograph revealed a large, nonhomogeneous opacity in the right hemithorax, denser in the middle and lower lung zones, with mild displacement of the mediastinum toward the left

node-6.label: Ultrasonography identified a large, heterogeneous, hypoechoic mass lesion in the right hemithorax with intratumoral vessels on Doppler; abdominal ultrasonography showed no evidence of abdominal mass or metastasis

attrs.why: New expert analyses confirm the right intrathoracic neoplastic mass: CECT shows a 20.8×13.6×13 cm heterogeneous mass with fat/calcification and compressive atelectasis, and biopsy reveals myxoid tissue, atypical cells, lipoblasts, S100+, and Alcian blue+ mucin. The pathologist confirms the mass and favors myxoid liposarcoma. These definitive imaging and pathologic findings increase confidence from 0.85 to 0.98; although molecular/PET/MRI data are absent for subtype/grade, the existence of a neoplastic mass is secure.

New CECT demonstrates a solid heterogeneous mass with fat/calcification and biopsy shows myxoid tumor tissue with lipoblasts; expert analyses explicitly refute pleural effusion/empyema. Combined with the absence of infectious symptoms and stable vitals, these findings make effusion/empyema highly unlikely, reducing confidence from 0.2 to 0.05.

CECT shows a pleural-based mass causing compressive atelectasis without invasion, and biopsy confirms myxoid lipomatous tumor. These findings indicate the lung parenchymal changes are secondary to the mass rather than primary lung parenchymal disease, reducing confidence from 0.1 to 0.05.
